request.spec:
A claim now has a status. It starts as DRAFT; it can be opened (OPEN) and then settled
(SETTLED); a DRAFT or OPEN claim can be voided (VOID). A SETTLED or VOID claim cannot change
status, and the buttons for a change that is not allowed are refused with an error on the claim.
Only OPEN and SETTLED claims count toward claimed, due-total and every total; drafts and voided
claims do not. Show each claim's status. Every status change writes an audit line: CLAIM_OPENED,
CLAIM_SETTLED or CLAIM_VOIDED, each with person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A claim now has a status. It starts as DRAFT; it can be opened (OPEN) and then settled
(SETTLED); a DRAFT or OPEN claim can be voided (VOID). A SETTLED or VOID claim cannot change
status, and the buttons for a change that is not allowed are refused with an error on the claim.
Only OPEN and SETTLED claims count toward claimed, due-total and every total; drafts and voided
claims do not. Show each claim's status. Every status change writes an audit line: CLAIM_OPENED,
CLAIM_SETTLED or CLAIM_VOIDED, each with person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Claims now have a status, and all 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`, including the audit-line checks.

**How it works**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V7__claim_status.sql`, adds a `status` column that defaults to `DRAFT` and only allows `DRAFT`, `OPEN`, `SETTLED` or `VOID`. Claims that already exist become drafts.
- **Server:** a new `ClaimStatus` enum holds the allowed changes: DRAFT→OPEN, OPEN→SETTLED, and DRAFT or OPEN→VOID. Each change has its own endpoint (`POST .../claims/{id}/open`, `/settle`, `/void`). `ClaimService.changeStatus` locks the claim row while it works, so if two users change the same claim at once, one change happens fully before the other. A change that isn't allowed gets a 409 and writes nothing. One that goes through writes `CLAIM_OPENED`, `CLAIM_SETTLED` or `CLAIM_VOIDED` with `person=… amount=… date=…` once it is saved. Claims returned by the API now include their status.
- **Front end:** each claim row shows `claim-status` and has Open, Settle and Void buttons. A refused change shows `claim-error` on that claim, and the error clears when you next act on the row. Claimed, due-total and both sheet totals now count only OPEN and SETTLED claims. Each claim's own `claim-due` is still shown whatever its status, as the test expects.

**Decisions you may want to revisit**
- **The server alone decides what's allowed.** I first had the screen refuse changes using its own copy of the claim. I took that out: if another user had just opened a draft, the screen would wrongly refuse a settle that the server would accept.
- **The buttons are always shown.** Not-allowed buttons stay visible and give an error when pressed, rather than being hidden, because the request asks for refused buttons to show an error on the claim.
- **Editing is unchanged.** The request doesn't say whether settled or voided claims can still be edited, so any claim can still be edited whatever its status.
